hook_text: In 1860 there was no South Africa. So what was on the map?
clip_script: Unroll a map of southern Africa in 1860. Two British colonies sit on the coasts: the Cape in the south-west, Natal in the east. Two Boer republics sit on the highveld, the Transvaal and the Orange Free State, set up by trekkers who left the Cape from 1835. And most of the map belongs to African kingdoms: the Zulu, the Swazi, Moshoeshoe's Basotho on their unconquered mountain, the Pedi, the Tswana, the Xhosa chiefdoms, the Mpondo, the Venda. They trade, they make treaties, they fight over land and cattle. Then, in 1867, a child picks up a shiny stone near the Orange River. Within fifty years, this map will be redrawn completely.
visual_style: A whiteboard outline of southern Africa filling with labelled patches of colour one by one, ending with a sparkling stone dropping onto the map.
pacing: An even rhythm, one region per beat, with a sharp cut on the stone.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the map of 1860 yourself.
